title: Advanced Analytics
tagline: PIVOT, LATERAL, advanced frames, sampling — analytics beyond GROUP BY

placementQuiz.q: PIVOT rotates rows to columns. In PostgreSQL, PIVOT is:
options: Done via crosstab() from tablefunc extension
placementQuiz.explain: PostgreSQL uses crosstab() from tablefunc extension for pivot. MySQL has PIVOT syntax in 8.0+.

placementQuiz.q: LATERAL join allows the right side to:
placementQuiz.explain: LATERAL allows right subquery to reference columns from left side of join.

placementQuiz.q: Advanced frame: ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING includes:
options: 2 rows before, current, 2 rows after (5 rows total)
placementQuiz.explain: 2 PRECEDING + current + 2 FOLLOWING = 5 rows total centered on current.
TABLESAMPLE SYSTEM samples at page level. Returns approximate percentage.

placementQuiz.q: LATERAL with LIMIT 1 for top-N per group — execution:
options: Index seek + LIMIT per outer row
placementQuiz.explain: LATERAL + ORDER BY + LIMIT 1 with index on (partition, order) = index seek + LIMIT per outer row.

sections.title: Mental Model — Analytics Beyond GROUP BY

blocks.md: GROUP BY collapses rows. Advanced analytics keeps rows but adds computed columns: PIVOT for cross-tabs, LATERAL for per-row subqueries, advanced frames for moving analytics, sampling for big data.

before.example: SELECT dept, AVG(sal) FROM emp GROUP BY dept

items: GROUP BY reduces rows; advanced analytics adds columns without collapsing
PIVOT/crosstab: row values become column headers (cross-tabulation)
LATERAL: correlated subquery in FROM clause — right side sees left columns
Sampling: TABLESAMPLE for approximate queries on massive tables

blocks.label: crosstab example
blocks.mysql:
-- MySQL 8.0+: PIVOT not native; use CASE + GROUP BY
SELECT dept,
  SUM(CASE WHEN quarter='Q1' THEN sales END) AS q1,
  SUM(CASE WHEN quarter='Q2' THEN sales END) AS q2
FROM sales GROUP BY dept;
blocks.py-pandas:
# pandas pivot_table
df.pivot_table(index='dept', columns='quarter', values='sales', aggfunc='sum')

blocks.text: LATERAL JOIN — Correlated Subquery in FROM

blocks.label: lateral basics
blocks.code:
-- For each employee, get latest order
SELECT e.name, o.order_date, o.total
FROM employees e
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT order_date, total
  FROM orders o
  WHERE o.emp_id = e.id
  ORDER BY o.order_date DESC
  LIMIT 1
) o ON true;

-- Equivalent correlated subquery (harder to read)
SELECT e.name,
  (SELECT order_date FROM orders o WHERE o.emp_id = e.id ORDER BY order_date DESC LIMIT 1) AS latest_date,
  (SELECT total FROM orders o WHERE o.emp_id = e.id ORDER BY order_date DESC LIMIT 1) AS latest_total
FROM employees e;
blocks.py-pandas:
# GroupBy + head(1)
latest = orders.sort_values('order_date').groupby('emp_id').head(1)
merged = employees.merge(latest, left_on='id', right_on='emp_id', how='left')

options: Columns from LEFT side of join
items.explain: LATERAL allows right side to see left side columns. Like correlated subquery in FROM.

items.q: CROSS JOIN LATERAL vs LEFT JOIN LATERAL:
options: CROSS = inner (drops left rows with no match), LEFT = preserves left
items.explain: CROSS JOIN LATERAL = INNER JOIN LATERAL. LEFT JOIN LATERAL preserves left rows (NULL if no match).

blocks.label: frame syntax
blocks.code:
-- ROWS: physical row count
SUM(amount) OVER (
  ORDER BY sale_date
  ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
) AS moving_sum_4days

-- RANGE: value-based (ORDER BY must be numeric/date)
SUM(amount) OVER (
  ORDER BY sale_date
  RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL '3 days' PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
) AS moving_sum_3days

-- Unbounded
SUM(amount) OVER (
  ORDER BY sale_date
  ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
) AS total_so_far
blocks.py-pandas:
# Rolling window
df['amount'].rolling(4).sum()  # 4-row window

# Date-based
from pandas import Timedelta
df.set_index('sale_date')['amount'].rolling(Timedelta('3D')).sum()

before.meaning: Current row + rows with ORDER BY value within 3

items.q: RANGE INTERVAL '1 day' PRECEDING with ORDER BY ts includes:
options: All rows where ts >= current_ts - 1 day
items.explain: RANGE uses value semantics. All rows with ts within 1 day of current row's ts.

items.q: ROWS 1 PRECEDING vs RANGE 1 PRECEDING with ORDER BY salary:
options: ROWS = 1 row before; RANGE = salaries within 1 of current
items.explain: ROWS counts rows. RANGE uses ORDER BY value difference (salary ± 1).

blocks.label: ntile
blocks.code:
-- Quartiles (4 buckets)
SELECT 
  name,
  salary,
  NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY salary) AS quartile
FROM employees;

-- Deciles (10 buckets)
SELECT 
  name,
  salary,
  NTILE(10) OVER (ORDER BY salary) AS decile
FROM employees;

-- Per department
SELECT 
  dept_id,
  name,
  salary,
  NTILE(4) OVER (PARTITION BY dept_id ORDER BY salary) AS dept_quartile
FROM employees;
blocks.py-pandas:
# Quantile bins
df['quartile'] = pd.qcut(df['salary'], 4, labels=[1,2,3,4])

# Per group
df['dept_quartile'] = df.groupby('dept_id')['salary'].transform(lambda x: pd.qcut(x, 4, labels=[1,2,3,4]))

blocks.md: NTILE distributes rows as evenly as possible. If rows % n ≠ 0, first buckets get 1 extra row. NTILE(4) on 10 rows → buckets: 3,3,2,2 rows.

blocks.label: filter clause / percentile
blocks.code:
-- FILTER: conditional aggregate in one scan
SELECT dept_id,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'active') AS active_cnt,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'pending') AS pending_cnt
FROM employees
GROUP BY dept_id;

-- Percentile aggregates
SELECT 
  percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY salary) AS median,
  percentile_disc(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY salary) AS median_discrete
FROM employees;

-- With GROUP BY
SELECT dept_id,
  percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY salary) AS median_sal
FROM employees
GROUP BY dept_id;
blocks.mysql:
-- MySQL 8.0+: no FILTER; use SUM(CASE...)
-- PERCENTILE_CONT/DISC in 8.0+

revisionCard: PIVOT/crosstab: rows → columns; PostgreSQL uses crosstab() from tablefunc
LATERAL: right side sees left columns; CROSS JOIN LATERAL = inner, LEFT JOIN LATERAL = outer
Frame clauses: ROWS = row count; RANGE = ORDER BY value distance; GROUPS = peer groups
NTILE(n) = n buckets; extra rows to first buckets
FILTER clause: conditional aggregate in one scan; cleaner than CASE

glossary.def: Right subquery references left columns. Like correlated subquery in FROM clause.
ROWS/RANGE/GROUPS BETWEEN ... defines window boundaries relative to current row.
Divides partition into n roughly equal buckets (1..n).
Fast approximate sampling of tables (SYSTEM = page-level, BERNOULLI = row-level).
